record.paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Recent Development
record.original_question: Study and classify null 2-type submanifolds, especially all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces. Here null 2-type means a 2-type immersion for which one of the two Laplace eigenvalues is zero; equivalently, its mean curvature vector H satisfies an equation of the form ΔH = λH with λ a nonzero real number.

evidence.quote: if all of the eigenvalues λ1,...,λk associated with the spectral decomposition are mutually different, then the immersion x (or the submanifold M) is said to be of k-type. In particular, if one of λ1,...,λk is zero, then the immersion is said to be of null k-type.
Problem 10. Study and classify null 2-type submanifolds. In particular, classify all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces.
It follows from the definition of null 2-type submanifolds and formula (2.3) that the mean curvature vector H of a null 2-type submanifold satisfies ΔH = λH, where λ is a nonzero real number.
However, until now there are still no complete classification of null 2-type submanifolds. In particular, null 2-type surfaces in Euclidean 4-space E^4 are not completely classified.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a connected submanifold of a (pseudo-)Euclidean space $\mathbb{E}^m_s$, isometrically immersed by $x:M\to\mathbb{E}^m_s$. The position vector $x$ admits a spectral decomposition with respect to the Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta$ of $M$. The immersion is said to be of $k$-type if $x$ can be written as
$$x = x_0 + x_{i_1} + x_{i_2} + \cdots + x_{i_k},$$
where $x_0$ is a constant vector and $\Delta x_{i_j} = \lambda_{i_j} x_{i_j}$ for $k$ pairwise distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_{i_1},\dots,\lambda_{i_k}\in\mathbb{R}$. The immersion is called null $k$-type if one of these eigenvalues equals $0$. Equivalently, $M$ is null $2$-type iff its mean curvature vector $H$ satisfies
$$\Delta H = \lambda H$$
for some nonzero constant $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$, while $M$ is not of $1$-type.

Problem: Study and classify all null $2$-type submanifolds. In particular, provide a complete classification of all null $2$-type surfaces in the Euclidean $4$-space $\mathbb{E}^4$ and in the pseudo-Euclidean $4$-spaces $\mathbb{E}^4_s$ ($s=1,2$).
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist (e.g., circular cylinders are the only null 2-type surfaces in $\mathbb{E}^3$, and classifications of $\delta(3)$-ideal null 2-type hypersurfaces and various special classes have been obtained), but a complete classification of null 2-type surfaces in $\mathbb{E}^4$ and in pseudo-Euclidean 4-spaces has not been achieved according to available sources.

status_evidence.title: δ(3)-ideal null 2-type hypersurfaces in Euclidean spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Every δ(3)-ideal null 2-type hypersurface in a Euclidean space has constant mean curvature and constant scalar curvature.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial classification results are available for null 2-type hypersurfaces; general classification in dimension 4 remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Null 2-type surfaces in Euclidean space
status_evidence.snippet: Study of null 2-type surfaces with partial classification.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues on null 2-type surfaces without a full classification in E^4.
